draft.title: Organic materials in everyday life
card: Organic compounds are built around carbon atoms, usually joined to hydrogen and often to oxygen, nitrogen or other elements. Many everyday materials are made of them.
Fabrics such as cotton, wool and nylon are organic. So are foods such as sugars, fats and proteins.
Many medicines, cosmetics and pesticides are organic compounds. Some come from living things and some are made in a laboratory.
Many parts of a car are organic too, such as tyres, seat fabric, paint and the plastic dashboard. Not every part is, because the metal body and the glass are not organic.
draft.remember: Organic compounds are in many things we wear, eat, use and drive.

a.q: Which of these everyday materials is made mainly of organic compounds?
a.why: Cotton is made of carbon-based compounds, so it is organic. Glass and salt are not built around carbon, and a steel body is mostly metal, so these are not organic.
a.clue: Which one is built around carbon compounds from a plant?

b.q: Ali's family car has the parts listed below. Which part is not made of organic compounds?
b.why: Steel is a metal, so it is not made of organic compounds. Rubber, paint and fabric are all organic. The tempting choice is the paint, but paint is made of organic compounds.
b.clue: Think about which part is a metal.

problems.detail: The clue 'built around carbon compounds from a plant' gives the answer away. Cotton is the only option that comes from a plant, so a student can pick it without knowing what makes a compound organic.
The clue 'Think about which part is a metal' gives the answer away. Steel is the only metal listed, so the student only needs to spot the metal, not understand organic compounds.
